title: Joint Learning of Energy-based Models and their Partition Function
reviewed_version: PMLR volume 267 published original; retrieved exact supplied PDF URL
summary: Local overbroad differentiability lemma; checked central scalar equivalence survives.

problems.title: Lemma 1 gradient assertion requires more than convexity
problems.claim: For every h, convex Omega+ with domain in positive measures implies equality of the displayed gradients.
assumptions: Omega+ is zero on the positive/nonnegative cone and infinity elsewhere
problems.check: Omega1*(h)=max(h1,h2); left and right derivatives along h1 are 0 and 1. Scalar minimization remains valid with tau*=max h.
problems.result: The displayed gradients need not exist.
problems.counterevidence: Main KL and strictly convex f-divergence applications impose stronger assumptions and have unique maximizers.
problems.impact: Local overstatement; no demonstrated damage to core KL/sparsemax equivalence or published experiments.
problems.correction: Restrict gradient identity to differentiable conjugates with a common maximizer; no blanket repair of full lemma claimed.

independent_acceptance_check.source_check: Read original PDF physical p16 Lemma 1, its quantifier for all h and Danskin proof; checked stronger generator restrictions in Proposition 4 (p7) and C.5.
independent_acceptance_check.hypotheses: Indicator of the nonnegative orthant is proper convex with domain in P_+(Y); Y={1,2}, h=(0,0) satisfy the lemma. If P_+ means strictly positive, the open-orthant variant has the same sup conjugates and the left gradient still fails.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: On the probability simplex, sup_p h.p=max(h1,h2); for h=(s,0), difference quotients are exactly 0 for s<0 and 1 for s>0. On the cone, the conjugate is 0 for z<=0 and infinity otherwise; min_tau tau+Omega_+*(h-tau) is max(h1,h2). Thus the scalar identity survives in this example while the asserted gradient cannot exist.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_dependency: The proof of Proposition 4 invokes Lemma 1 but has a strictly convex generator, excluded by this indicator example. KL elimination gives H(t)=t+Ze^-t-Q with minimizer log Z and finite positive Hessian. No central-invalidity inference from the weaker lemma was made. The Eq17 counting/probability normalization discussion is appropriately a convention clarification.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_and_repair: Minor retained: demonstrated auxiliary overstatement; no counterexample to the stated core strictly convex case. Restricting the gradient identity to differentiable conjugates with a common attained maximizer makes both gradients that maximizer, but does not fix unconstrained general strong-duality/attainment issues.
